title: Gulf Coast string outfit and the original Owls personnel
summary: The instruments and members of the summer hotel group, then the five original Owls and later additions at the Roosevelt.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Oh yeah. Oh, that Ogden fellow, I didn't get what instrument he played over there.
So you had a banjo and a drum.
We had, it was a funny thing, we had a banjo, a guitar, two violins, and Guy Lyman on this contraption he had, it wasn't a drum, it was just a box with a bunch of plates on it that he would beat on.
Who was the guitar player again? Was that Mark Smith?
No, no, no, that wasn't. That was Jinx DeBall or Eugene DeBall.

He's a, I think he's an architect here in town now. And Ogden was with the Bonds Department of one of the banks, I haven't seen him in years so I don't know what he's doing now. and Ogden was, was, well he wrote some of the funniest little pieces of music with words to it that, they were just cute pieces that's all and that was, as we used those to entertain the people at these two hotels over there. That was a forerunner to the, to the Owls. The original Owls was composed, the actual original Owls was composed of, of the two Mackey boys Red Mackey, Dick Mackey, Monk Smith, Eblin Rao, and myself. That was the original, original Owls. Later, Moe's fair came in on the piano and Red Mackey went to the bass and later, Moe's, well Moe's was with us at the Roosevelt Hotel but then we brought in another piano player called, Sig Christiansen, who made, quite a few of these recordings with us. A fellow, another trumpet player came with us too was Red Bowman, who was with us for a while. The original Owls were those five that I named and then of course we, when we got into the Roosevelt Hotel, Pinky came in, Dan LeBlanc came in on the bass and, well, Billy Burton came in as a, a leader. He wasn't with us so more than just a few months. Just a few months.
